editorial.thesis: A learning-and-hospitality city of about 1.4 million. Its retail is heavy on fitness & wellness and coaching & training, and thin on grocery & daily needs and apparel, footwear & jewellery — and 28% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is ahead of Delhi. 26.58 chain outlets per lakh residents against 18.83 in Delhi; 37 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Café Coffee Day 43, Subway 33, Domino's 29.

The mapped economy leans to education. Shares of all mapped places: education 9.9% (Delhi 7.9%); hotels & stays 5.5% (Delhi 4.4%); grocery & daily needs 1.3% (Delhi 2.2%); malls & department stores 0.6% (Delhi 0.8%). Raw counts would mislead because Delhi is mapped more completely (87,703 places against 21,465), so we compare mix, not counts.

Supply and demand are misaligned. 4 zones hold 28% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Dakshin Marg · Main Market alone has about 120,000 residents and 67 mapped food & drink places.

Retail is less concentrated than in Delhi. 46% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Delhi 47%). The largest cores are Himalaya Marg · Dakshin Marg (1,258 places) and Ram Darbar (1,198).

The widest brand gaps against Delhi. Domino's 29 outlets vs 140; Café Coffee Day 43 outlets vs 145; Apollo Pharmacy 20 outlets vs 108. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 8 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Delhi, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Manimajra and Dakshin Marg · Main Market are the largest zones by residents (121,000 and 120,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 46% of all commercial places, and Himalaya Marg · Dakshin Marg alone lists 1,258.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Ram Darbar holds 38 of the 379 tracked chain outlets, and Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar · Sas Nagar adds 33.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Himalaya Marg · Dakshin Marg and Dakshin Marg · Main Market lead on education places (283 and 175, with 129 and 65 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Dakshin Marg · Main Market and Dadu Majra Colony. The blue cores include Himalaya Marg · Dakshin Marg.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (87,703 places in Delhi against 21,465 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Delhi; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Delhi, Chandigarh's mapped places over-index on education (9.9% vs 7.9%), hotels & stays (5.5% vs 4.4%), healthcare (8.2% vs 6.9%) and under-index on grocery & daily needs (1.3% vs 2.2%), malls & department stores (0.6% vs 0.8%), shops & retail (12.8% vs 17.2%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 379 outlets of 37 tracked national brands within 8 km — 26.58 per lakh residents against Delhi's 18.83 (1289 outlets of 45 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Delhi are Domino's (29 vs 140); Café Coffee Day (43 vs 145); Apollo Pharmacy (20 vs 108). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Delhi's, so low means thin by Delhi's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 8 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Chandigarh's age mix against Delhi: children (0–14) 22.7% vs 23.1%, 15–24 21.1% vs 20.4%, working age 49.5% vs 49.7%, 60+ 6.7% vs 6.8%. Under-25s are 44% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 5.4% of mapped places against 5.7% in Delhi, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Subway 33 (Delhi 55), Domino's 29 (Delhi 140), Pizza Hut 26 (Delhi 68), KFC 17 (Delhi 51).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 2.1% of mapped places against 2.1% in Delhi, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 43 (Delhi 145), Starbucks 6 (Delhi 33), Chaayos 6 (Delhi 18), Third Wave Coffee 6 (Delhi 13).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.6% of mapped places against 0.7% in Delhi, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 24 (Delhi 29). No mapped outlet in either city: Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.3% of mapped places against 2.2% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 9 (Delhi 21), More 4 (Delhi 2), DMart 3 (Delhi 7), Big Bazaar 2 (Delhi 8). No mapped outlet in either city: Star Bazaar.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 0.9% of mapped places against 1.2% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 20 (Delhi 108). No mapped outlet in either city: MedPlus, Wellness Forever, Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 5.1% of mapped places against 7.0% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 25 (Delhi 66), Raymond 20 (Delhi 55), Tanishq 8 (Delhi 20), Reliance Trends 7 (Delhi 22).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 6.8% of mapped places against 7.9% in Delhi — below its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 3.1% of mapped places against 2.7% in Delhi — above its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 5.6% of mapped places against 3.9% in Delhi — above its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
